text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BUSINESS LEADERS CREATE 'BLOC' WITHIN MERCOSUR

Brazilian and Argentine business leaders took advantage of the Free Trade Area of the Americas talks in Belo Horizonte to agree on the creation of a private sector 'bloc' within the Mercosur customs union which will discuss macroeconomic issues on a regular basis.
-- HSBC DOES NOT WANT PRICE WAR

HSBC Bamerindus President Michael Geoghegan said contrary to expectations the bank had no intention of starting a price war between Brazilian retail banks because this could hurt the banks' capital base.
-- ACCUSATION UNSETTLES THE MARKET

No political episode under President Cardoso's administration has unsettled the financial markets as much as newspaper allegations that Communications Minister Sergio Motta is involved in a cash-for-votes scandal.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- DEPUTY SAYS ON TAPE MOTTA GAVE HIM TV CONCESSION

Deputy Ronivon Santiago, who has admitted to selling his vote for money, said in another taped conversation that Communications Minister Sergio Motta granted him a television and radio concession in exchange for his vote.
-- MOTTA REJECTS ACCUSATIONS AND WILL SUE

Communications Minister Sergio Motta has rejected all allegations that he paid off deputies so they would vote in favor of a bill allowing President Cardoso to stand for re-election, saying he will sue the deputies who made the accusations.
-- CARDOSO WILL DISMISS THOSE GUILTY OF CASH-FOR-VOTE DEAL

President Cardoso said he did not believe Communications Minister Sergio Motta was involved in the cash-for-votes scandal, but that he would dismiss any member of the government whose involvement in the deal could be proved.
O GLOBO
-- COMMISSION CALLS MINISTER AND GOVERNORS FOR STATEMENT

The congressional commission investigating the cash-for-votes scandal involving Communications Minister Sergio Motta, two state governors and five deputies has asked Motta and the governors to make a statement.
-- CARDOSO INTERFERES WITH POLICE OVER VANDALISM

President Cardoso lost his patience and intervened with military police in Brasilia who spent all day trying to dislodge a group of small farmers who invaded the Planning Ministry with an entourage of animals to stage a protest.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
